full_judgment:
Mr. A. B. M. Khairul Haque J.:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1 to 11, to show cause as to why the Order No. 68 dated 8.7.1987 and Order No. 74 dated 30.7.1987 passed by the Assistant Judge,- Birganj, Dinajpur, in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1985, should not be se aside. 

 3. During pendency of the suit, it was transferred to the Court of Munsif, Birganj and was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 5 of 1984. On 12.12.1984, the heirs of the plaintiff filed an application before the said Court, disclosing the death of Amjad Hossain, the sole plaintiff and prayed for substituting them as his legal heirs. The learned Judge after hearing, by his order lip dated: 15.1.1985, rejected their said petition and recorded abatement of the suit. On 9.2.1985, the opposite party nos. 1 to 11 filed an application under Order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for their addition as the plaintiffs in the said suit. They also filed another application under Section 151 of the Code, for adding them as heirs of the sole plaintiff after vacating the order of abatement dated 15.1.1985. The learned Munsif by his Order no. 18 dated 7.4.1985, rejected the petition under Order I rule 10 of the Code on the ground that the suit being abated, was no longer in existence for their addition therein. He, however, treated the application filed under Section 151 of the Code as one under Order XXII rule 9 of the Code and was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1985. The said Miscellaneous Case was contested on behalf of the petitioners. After closing of the evidence, on 8.7.1987, the opposite party nos. 1 to 11 filed an application for amendment of the petition of the miscellaneous case in order to insert the date of death of Amjad Hossain as on 28.7.1984. The learned Judge allowed the said petition for amendment by Order no. 68 dated 8.7.1987. The petitioner also filed an application for recalling one of the witnesses: The said prayer was also allowed. On the same date the additional written statement was filed on behalf of the petitioners which were also accepted. Thereafter the learned Judge heard the arguments on behalf of both the parties on the same date on 8.7.1987. In due course, by his Judgment and Order dated 30.7.1987, the learned Judge allowed the miscellaneous case, set-aside the order of abatement dated 15.1.1985 and restored the Other Class Suit to its file and number. Being aggrieved, by the Order no. 68, allowing amendment and also in allowing the miscellaneous case, the petitioners obtained the present Rule. 

 7. In reply Mr. Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the case of the petitioners before the learned Assistant Judge was that the sole plaintiff died on 28.7.1984 and not on 28.9.1984, that this fact, he submitted was substantiated by filing as many as three certificates and also through one of the witnesses, namely, Dr. Moijuddin that the sole plaintiff died on 28.7.1984 but on the other hand no effort was taken on behalf of the opposite party nos. 1 to 11, to show the correct date of death of the sole plaintiff. 

 9. It appears that in Other Class Suit No. 25 of 1980, Amjad Hossain was the sole plaintiff. The opposite party nos. 1 to 11 stated in their petition dated 12.12.1984 that Amjad Hossain died on 28.9.1984. This was their consistent case. Subsequently, a certificate to that effect was also filed as appearing from their petition on 8.7.1987 and order No. 68 dated 8.7.1987. But on the other hand the petitioners always maintained that the sole plaintiff died on 28.7.1984. They stated so in another appeal pending between the parties namely, Miscellaneous. Appeal No. 6 of 1984, pending in the Court of District Judge Dinajpur. Besides one of their witnesses Dr. Moyezuddin Ahmed, also stated that the sole plaintiff died on 28.7.1984. 

 10. The learned Assistant Judge, however, did not give much importance to the date of death in deciding the issue of abatement before him. He, rather, considered the fact that because of the transfer of the suit from one Court to another, the petitioners in the miscellaneous case were prevented by sufficient cause in making the necessary petition in time for substitution. 

 In this connection, it should be noted that the petition was filed beyond the period of 90 days but within the period of next 60 days, praying only for impleading the heirs left by the sole plaintiff, presumably under Order XXII rule 3 of the Code instead of rule 9(2). In the said petition although not formally prayed, in so many words, for setting aside abatement but it should be so treated by the Court, instead of rejecting it, as in this case, because ultimately it is for the Court and not the litigants, to apply the correct provisions of law in the given facts and Circumstances. Reliance in this regard is made in the case of Vijavasing Dattajirao Thorat V. Shivajirao Narayanrao AIR 1924 Born 416. 

 In the present case also the learned. Judge ought to have treated the petition dated 12.12.1984 as one under Order XXII rule 9(2) of the Code. This would have shorten the process. He, however, ultimately did so in respect of the petition dated 9.2.1985.
